title: Japan Airport Customs to Be 100% Digital by 2030
paragraphs: As the number of foreign tourists visiting Japan continues to grow, the country's airports are under increasing pressure. To make arrival smoother, Japan's Finance Ministry has announced plans to make customs declarations at airports fully digital by 2030.

When travelers arrive in Japan, they must make a declaration to customs about the items they are bringing into the country, including both the luggage they carry with them and items sent separately. Japan introduced electronic customs declarations in 2019, allowing travelers to complete the process online. However, as of April 2026, around half of all declarations were still being submitted on paper.

Under the new plan, which was reported in June 2026, the entire process will move online. Passengers will enter information such as their names and addresses online in advance, and then use a QR code to complete the procedure when they arrive. According to the ministry, the change is intended to make entry more convenient for travelers and to reduce the workload of customs officers. Electronic gates for customs are already in operation at several major airports, including Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu, Fukuoka, New Chitose and Naha.
The plan is part of a broader strategy, known as "Customs Vision 2030," which also includes using artificial intelligence to inspect small packages with X-ray machines at major airports.

The move reflects the rapid growth of tourism in Japan. In 2025, the number of foreign visitors exceeded 40 million for the first time, reaching a record of about 42.7 million, and the government aims to attract 60 million visitors a year by 2030.

In addition, the government is planning to introduce an electronic travel authorization system, similar to the American ESTA, for visitors who do not need a visa. Under this system, travelers would need to apply online before their trip. Some reports suggest that the system could begin before 2028.
Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether paper forms will be completely abolished, so travelers are advised to check the latest information before their trip.
